title: Minimax ATE Estimation under Joint Heavy Outcome Tails and Power-Law Propensity Decay

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched rate proposal for all-estimator ATE risk and honest connected-interval length under a conditional moment envelope and polynomial overlap, then extended the candidate to q >= 2 by a binary-law saturation argument. The D0.5 cold referee rated the sharply specified benchmark subfield, below the required field floor, and found no bounded in-scope novelty lift. Its math and positioning panels also returned unrepaired REVISE findings on the saturation proposition; no formalization or Lean verification occurred, and this bank is not a soundness certificate.
tldr: Let \(q_\star=\min\{q,2\}\). For every fixed finite \(q>1\), the full-population ATE is estimable over the conditional-moment power-propensity class at the matching all-estimator absolute-risk and finite-sample honest connected-interval expected-length order \(r_n(q_\star,\kappa)\): \(n^{-(q_\star-1)/q_\star}\) below \(\kappa(q_\star-1)=1\), the same power times \(\{\log(en)\}^{1/q_\star}\) at equality, and \(n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\) above it. For \(1<q\le2\), a split-sample scale estimate, trimmed inverse-probability mean, clipping, and Markov calibration attain the rate, while a coordinated rare-mark pair gives the exact full-record total-variation converse. For \(q\ge2\), conditional Lyapunov reduces achievability to the \(q=2\) procedure and bounded binary full-record alternatives give both converses, so precision saturates at the second-moment elbow. The binary branch motivates the Sasaki--Ura robustate right-heart-catheterization use case without asserting an exact power propensity for those data.
gap: Khan and Tamer's primary weak-overlap ATE analysis proves a zero information bound and derives nonregular rates for a trimmed inverse-weighted estimator in selected tail examples, but it does not characterize all-estimator minimax risk or all-honest-connected-interval expected length. Other results regularize the outcome regression, impose score-tail regularity, optimize intervals under Gaussian smoothness restrictions, or control generic weighted rewards. None of the inspected theorem texts gives the all-law conditional-\(q\) ATE frontier with its equality-case logarithm.
fill: The project pairs a fully observed-data rare-mark modulus with an explicit estimator and finite-sample interval, proving the same three-regime order for all estimators and all honest connected intervals; a separate Bernoulli full-record experiment supplies the binary \(q=2\) lower frontier through the critical \(\kappa=1\) boundary.
